persistent_identifier_status: Repository-local stable dataset identifier. The companion journal article DOI is linked; no separate dataset DOI was identified.
title: Elemental and energy-quality summary of press cake from Kassel roadside-grass IFBB processing
citation: Piepenschneider, M., Bühle, L., Hensgen, F., & Wachendorf, M. (2016). Energy recovery from grass of urban roadside verges by anaerobic digestion and combustion after pre-processing. Biomass and Bioenergy, 85, 194–202. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biombioe.2015.12.012. Values transcribed from Table 12 of Piepenschneider, M. (2015), Urban Grass and Grass-Leaf Litter Mixtures as Source for Bioenergy Recovery, University of Kassel dissertation.
source_locations: Dissertation Chapter 4 Table 12, printed p. 56 (PDF p. 67); methods for press cake sampling and calorific-value calculations, printed pp. 45–47 (PDF pp. 56–58)
license: No explicit open reuse license identified for the thesis or article. This dataset contains a limited attributed transcription of published table values; verify rights before external redistribution.
material_scope: IFBB press cake from 2-cut urban roadside grass, reported separately for first and second harvest.
experimental_conditions: Silage from 2-cut material was mixed with warm water at 40 C and a 1:4 fresh-matter ratio for 15 minutes, then screw-pressed. Press cake was dried at 65 C for elemental analysis; DM was separately determined at 105 C. Table 12 reports n=10 first-cut and n=5 second-cut samples. The source states that between-cut significance tests were not conducted because of unequal sample counts and non-random second-cut samples from sites with high growth.
data_scope: 14 rows: mean and standard deviation for C, H, N, HHV, LHV, ash, and K2O/CaO ratio for both harvests. HHV and LHV are calculated by the source, not directly measured calorimetry.
limitations: Kassel press cake is a process-specific German comparator; it does not establish GreenHub press-cake composition or product grade.
Second-cut samples were selected from sites with sufficient growth and were non-random; there is no statistical comparison between cuts.
HHV and LHV are source-calculated from elemental composition; LHV is calculated from HHV and hydrogen content.
The table reports a K2O/CaO ratio without the underlying paired oxide measurements.
No downstream drying-energy, product moisture, market grade, emissions, or commercial saleability is established.
Reference-only. No runtime property, equation, or default is activated.
conversion_or_processing: Values and reported standard deviations transcribed as printed. No conversion, pooling, imputation, or process scaling was performed.
uncertainty: Source-reported SD values are preserved. Between-cut significance was not tested.
